issues.title: Issue 363: Wagtail's new API
issues.html:
News

In Memoriam: Tim Peters, 1952-2026

Guido van Rossum shared the news that Tim Peters died on July 15. He wrote the Zen of Python (PEP 20) and gave Python Timsort, and as "Timbot" he answered countless questions and set the tone for early core development. Pythonistas are sharing their memories in the thread.

Wagtail CMS News

DRF vs Django Ninja: the Wagtail 8.1 API schema

Wagtail's new API runs on Django Ninja, not DRF, and Sage Abdullah and Thibaud Colas explain why: schema generation is first-party rather than deprecated in favor of drf-spectacular, and Pydantic schemas follow the type hints Wagtail already uses.

Djangonaut Space News

Picking Up Django #26355, Part 1: Understanding the Problem

Emanuel Jaimes explores Django ticket #26355, investigating previous implementation attempts and possible approaches to supporting PostgreSQL's array_append functionality in ArrayField.

Landing My First Commit in Django Core.

Goodluck Igbokwe shares his journey to his first Django core commit, exploring ImageField validation and the importance of understanding the code behind the documentation.

Python Software Foundation

Python 3.16.0 alpha 2 is now available

uuid4() and uuid7() now have C implementations and run 15-30x faster, re picked up nested character sets, and startup and garbage collection are quicker. Alpha 3 follows on December 15.

PyPI's redesigned project pages with clearer security signals are now live

Each PyPI project now has a Security tab that shows whether a release has full provenance, meaning every file has an attestation, or none. The redesign also adds search and filters to the release files list, and shows file counts and yanked or quarantined status in the release history.

Joshua Mcshannon Joins the PSF as Infrastructure Engineer

The PSF's new Infrastructure Engineer will spend his time cutting operational toil across python.org, PyPI, and the systems behind PyCon US. He has already started on Kubernetes cost savings.

Updates to Django

Today, "Updates to Django" is presented by Raffaella from Djangonaut Space! 🚀

Last week we had 17 pull requests merged into Django by 15 different contributors - including 8 first-time contributors! Congratulations to ines besrour, himanshu0870, ShabirAhmadLinux, Patel Namraa, Dmitry, Sahil Advani, Kunal Kumar and Hossein Shams for having their first commits merged into Django - welcome on board!

New in Django 6.2:

  • An input_type of "textarea" was added to the Textarea widget. Like other widgets, when set to "hidden" it now renders the hidden HTML attribute. (PR #21857)
  • django is now the preferred name for Django's command-line interface. django-admin remains available as an alias. Both names provide the same functionality. (PR #21260)

New in Django 6.1:

  • Fixed a bug in Django 6.1 where accessing a deferred field with the FETCH_PEERS fetch mode overwrote values that peer instances had already modified locally or loaded via refresh_from_db with an explicit fields argument. The fix also addresses a KeyError when a peer's row had been deleted (#37436).

Django Fellow Reports

Django Fellow Report - Jacob

Between release blocker and security work, Jacob ran a small Trac sprint over Sarah's triage workflow changes and this year's Google Summer of Code dark mode project, and followed up with the GDAL maintainers on findings from the security releases. The main management command is now named django.

Django Fellow Report - Sarah

A four-day week spent mostly on triage and the "Ready for Checkin" backlog, accepting tickets on StepValueValidator crashing for large numbers, order_by("pk") on a union of composite-pk models, and NegatedExpression mishandling FullResultSet. She also enforced ticket assignment limits and triage restrictions in Trac.

Sponsored

Prod-like data for your coding agents

Coding agents write Django code against fixtures and guess what your data looks like. Baseshift gives every agent, PR and developer its own masked copy of your production database, ready in seconds, with no infrastructure changes. Start free and point DATABASE_URL at your first clone.

Articles

Django's Generic Views: FormView

Ben Cardy's fourth class-based view post walks through FormView, which renders a form, validates it, and redirects on success.

Making Django admin easier to use every day

Some examples of a team customizing the admin as needed for their specific use cases. A worthwhile effort if you use it heavily.

Django: introducing django-launch-editor for jump-to-file debugging

Adam Johnson's new package makes the file paths on Django's debug page clickable, opening your editor right at that line. When the editor is out of reach, in Docker or on a server, clicking copies the location instead.

Authenticating Django Channels WebSockets without putting the JWT in the URL

A browser cannot send an Authorization header on a WebSocket handshake. The common fix puts the token in the query string, where every access log keeps a copy. This is the other way, and the four places it can quietly go wrong.

Using OpenTofu to manage your Infrastructure as Code

Ryan Cheley finally learned the OpenTofu that Django Commons runs on by importing his own AWS, Coolify, DigitalOcean, GitHub, Hetzner, and Tailscale setup.

Lock your GitHub Actions

Action tags can be moved, so a workflow pinned to a safe-looking tag can start running an attacker's code. Hugo van Kemenade walks through GitHub's new workflow lockfiles.

Catch the import. Name the culprit. Keep threads free: Introducing gilguard

gilguard is a tiny, zero-dependency package for free-threaded Python (3.13t, 3.14t, 3.15t). Import it first. If any later import quietly turns the GIL back on, you get an error naming the extension module, the package that shipped it, and the line of your code that pulled it in.

What makes uv slow?

uv maintainer Konstin walks through where uv still spends its time, from source distribution builds and network requests down to TOML parsing (about 30ms just to read Airflow's lockfile), hashing, NTFS, and memory allocation.

Events

Wagtail Space 2026

Wagtail Space is next week, November 18-20. The event is 100% online and you can watch live or watch the recordings at your convenience. Expect talks from Wagtail and Django experts plus guest speakers on AI, sustainable tech, and other trends shaping the web. Tickets are free, so grab one before Wednesday.

Videos

People First, Code Always - Kenneth Love

Longtime Django developer Kenneth is the guest in this episode from Jon Gould at Foxley Talent. Lots of insights from coding in the pre/post AI world.

Databases, Django APIs, and AI - Haki Benita

The video cut of Django Chat #209, just over an hour with Haki Benita on getting more out of the ORM and PostgreSQL indexes, where Django Ninja fits, and what Django still needs for typing and APIs. That last part is the ground DEP 0017 covers, adding content type parsing and a request.data attribute that handles JSON, and the forum thread has the wider debate.

Django Job Board

The PSF's CPython Developer in Residence opening is still accepting applications, alongside senior Python roles at Manychat in Barcelona and Proxify, plus a founding engineering role at Alloy.

CPython Developer in Residence at Python Software Foundation

Senior Python Engineer (Barcelona-based / Relocation support to Barcelona) at Manychat

Senior Backend Developer (Python) at Proxify AB

Founding Forward Deployed Engineer at Alloy

Projects

prafulgulani/django-experimental

A playground for trying experimental Django features behind feature flags, installed as django.experimental.

swarfte/django-ninja-expose

Add @expose() to a Django model. Get a REST API.

issues.title: Issue 362: Django 6.1.3, 6.0.10, and 5.2.19 Security Releases
issues.html:
News

Django security releases issued: 6.1.3, 6.0.10, and 5.2.19

Six CVEs, three of them in GeoDjango: two server-side request forgery holes where GDAL resolved URLs or files from GeoJSON CRS members and SpatialReference strings (full protection needs GDAL 3.9+, flagged by the new gis.W001 check), plus log injection through GeometryField. The rest cover base64 uploads that ignored FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE, cache keys that confused missing and empty Vary headers, and password hashes shown to view-only admin users. Upgrade soon.

Django Software Foundation

Django Steering Council Meeting, November 2

The Steering Council met with the Fellows ahead of the mid-January feature freeze, with Carlton Gibson aiming to land the async transactions PR before then. They also weighed what to do now that sqlparse is no longer maintained (it backs --debug-sql and inspectdb), how to surface DEP discussions on the Forum, and GSoC 2027 ideas.

Python Software Foundation

Announcing new Security Developer at the PSF

Brett Smith, formerly of the W3C and Software Freedom Conservancy, joins Seth Larson and Mike Fiedler on the PSF security team in a new role funded by Anthropic. The Python Security Response Team is handling 3-4× last year's volume of reports and CVEs, and PyPI malware is up 60%, so Brett will help with remediation and scale PyPI's autonomous quarantine program.

How the Python ecosystem responded to the eMudhra intermediate compromise

Within two days of the October 20 CA compromise, fixes shipped for certifi, Python, pip, uv, sigstore, virtualenv, and more, and Python added a last-resort denylist for the bad intermediates (CVE-2026-115557) that was backported to older releases. Seth Larson explains why certifi, pip, and Python sat in the critical path, and why browsers were safe from day one thanks to certificate revocation lists, which Python may adopt.

Wagtail CMS News

Wagtail 8.1: automate more with an improved API and agent-ready tools

The preview REST API can now write more content types, expose StreamField block schemas, and drive moderation workflows (submit, approve, reject, cancel), alongside official agent skills and a prototype CLI. Editors also get SEO checks for meta titles and descriptions, pages can be served as JSON or Markdown from the same URL, and multilingual sitemaps now include translated pages.

An official headless demo for Wagtail

bakerydemo-headless rebuilds the bakery demo as a fully decoupled Next.js front-end in TypeScript, with live preview still working in the CMS. Thibaud Colas notes it runs about 95% on Wagtail's built-in v3 API, whose OpenAPI schema generates typed clients down to individual StreamField blocks, with no GraphQL required.

Updates to Django

Today, "Updates to Django" is presented by Hwayoung from Djangonaut Space! 🚀

Last week we had 17 pull requests merged into Django by 12 different contributors - including 2 first-time contributors! Congratulations to Alex Henman and Spoko Dev for having their first commits merged into Django - welcome on board!

News in Django:

  • Django now supports the HTTP QUERY method, allowing safe, idempotent requests with query content in the request body (#37232).
  • Django templates now support template tags spanning multiple lines, making tags with several arguments easier to read (#35899).
  • Fixed a regression where BoundField.legend_tag() could add a custom required CSS class more than once when passed attrs (#37463).

Django Fellow Reports

Django Fellow Report - Jacob

Jacob Tyler Walls finalized the patches and sent prenotifications for Django's November security releases, then started drafting patches for the next round. He also fixed attrs mutation in legend_tag(), opened a follow-up optimizing lookup preparation for GeoJSON geometries, and sat in on Executive Director interviews.

Django Fellow Report - Sarah

Sarah Boyce accepted five tickets, including consistent database selection for subqueries, dropping GIS support on 32-bit Windows, and a parallel test runner crash, and reviewed fixes for XOR join promotion, select_for_update() after combined queries, and warning assertions. Her own PR allowing multiline template tags was merged, and she worked on three security reports and interviewed final candidates for Executive Director.

Django Fellow Report - Natalia

Natalia Bidart prepared the branch that bootstraps Django 2028, the first calendar-versioned release: it drops Python 3.12 and 3.13, removes the EMAIL_* settings in favor of MAILERS, and finalizes several ORM deprecations, and it lands in mid-January once the 6.2 branch is cut. She also pushed docs PRs that give local builds a new theme and better accessibility, and joined three Executive Director interviews.

Sponsored

Django for Beginners, 6th Edition

The sixth edition is out now, available in digital and paperback formats. It features two new chapters, completely updated for Django 6.1+, and more. Read the first four chapters for free to try it out.

Articles

Soft delete in Django without making a mess

Stein Ove Helset builds soft delete on a deleted_at timestamp and works through where it breaks: bulk QuerySet.delete() still removes rows, unique=True blocks re-creating a deleted record (a conditional UniqueConstraint fixes that, though MySQL and MariaDB ignore the condition), restores can collide with newer rows, and CASCADE never fires for related objects. A filtered default manager paired with an unfiltered base manager keeps related lookups working.

N+1 queries in Django Admin

If a related model's __str__ reads another foreign key, every option in an admin dropdown runs its own query, and select_related() on the edited object doesn't reach those options. Override formfield_for_foreignkey() and formfield_for_manytomany() to add select_related() to the querysets behind the widgets.

Django's Generic Views: TemplateView

Ben Cardy's series on class-based views reaches TemplateView, which needs only a template_name. He uses extra_context for static values, get_context_data() for computed ones, and template_engine to render a single view with Jinja2.

Taking Website Screenshots with Django, Celery, and Playwright

Nik Tomazic builds a Dockerized Django app that takes full-page or viewport screenshots with Playwright. Each capture runs in a Celery task so the form returns right away, and the page polls a small JSON status view until the image is ready. An optional last section moves the browser to Browser Use's paid hosted Chromium for when local browsers eat worker memory or hit bot detection.

Looking for a job? Start a blog.

Tim Schilling argues that a blog shows a hiring manager how you communicate before they ever talk to you, and suggests starter topics like a recent technical decision or how you review code. He says the host doesn't matter (GitHub Pages, dev.to, and Medium all work) and asks you to write it yourself instead of with AI, since the point is to show how you think.

How Caktus Runs and Uses Local Models

Tobias McNulty and Colin Copeland describe the two-GPU workstation Caktus uses to serve open-weight models over Tailscale, so client code stays on its own network. A dense Qwen3.8-27B handles planning and long sessions, and a Qwen3.6 MoE with 3B active parameters runs everyday work at 200-250 tokens per second, both on vLLM in Docker Compose. The post includes their benchmarks, why Gemma 4 31B didn't make the cut, and the pi.dev and VS Code configs they use daily.

Per-Object Permissions in Django That Roll Back with Atomic()

Joshua Fields wrote pemba, a Zanzibar-style authorization library that keeps per-object permission relationships in your own Django database. A grant is just rows in the current transaction, so it commits or rolls back with the data it protects, which a separate service like SpiceDB can't guarantee.

Artisanal Podcasting in the Age of AI

Will Vincent has hand-edited Django Chat in GarageBand for nearly seven years, even with AI tools that promise to handle the whole thing. Editing gives him a second listen to each conversation and a kind of deep focus he no longer gets when coding with a handful of AI agents.

Caching at Scale in Django: Lessons from Production

Johnny Metz's team handled about 20x traffic growth on a multi-tenant Django API by caching aggressively: per-user lists of document IDs paired with one shared entry per document, seven-day TTLs with invalidation on Django signals, a cached identity lookup, and failing open when Redis goes down. During the rollout, database queries per second halved, and Redis now serves most reads at a 97% hit rate.

Events

DjangoCon Europe 2027 Call for Participation

DjangoCon Europe runs February 17-21, 2027, in Innsbruck, Austria, and wants talk and workshop proposals on technical and non-technical topics from new and experienced speakers. Proposals close November 15, 2026.

Podcasts

Django Chat #209: Databases, Django APIs, and AI - Haki Benita

Haki Benita talks about getting more out of Django's ORM and PostgreSQL indexes, why Django Ninja appeals for APIs, and what Django needs for typing and a built-in API story. They also get into how AI is changing the way developers learn and share what they know.

Videos

From librarian to Djangonaut: My Open Source journey with Annabelle Wiegart

In a guest talk for Djangonaut Space Session 7, Annabelle Wiegart traces her path from librarian to Django contributor, PyLadies Zurich organizer, and Djangonaut Space captain. She talks about working on ORM tickets and nullable expressions with mentors, and how contributing went from intimidating to something she could do.

Django Forum

A Path to Modernizing APIs in Django (DEP 0017 Content Type Parsing)

Picking up from the Haki Benita episode of Django Chat, Will Vincent lists what stands between Django and a built-in API: a modernized HttpRequest through DEP 0017, a pluggable serialization layer (the hardest part), and then the view layer. Carlton Gibson wants those primitives updated first, while Haki would settle on an official API interface and tune performance later.

Django Job Board

The PSF's CPython Developer in Residence opening leads the board this week, alongside senior Python roles at webbyfox consultancy and at Manychat in Barcelona, with relocation support.

CPython Developer in Residence at Python Software Foundation

Senior Python Engineer at webbyfox consultancy

Senior Python Engineer (Barcelona-based / Relocation support to Barcelona) at Manychat

Projects

amureki/django-cmdbar

Adds a Cmd+K / Ctrl+K palette to the Django admin for jumping to models, searching records (user alice), or opening one by primary key (user#42). It respects admin permissions and needs no frontend dependencies, middleware, URLs, or migrations: just add django_cmdbar above django.contrib.admin in INSTALLED_APPS.

Metron-Project/izaya

An htmx-powered autocomplete widget for Django forms that ships no required styles, so it fits any CSS framework. Register a ModelLookup with your search_fields, drop LookupWidget into a form (with multiple=True for multi-selects), and use rank_fields to put the closest matches first; it needs Python 3.14+ and Django 6.0+.

issues.title: Issue 361: DjangoCon Europe and DjangoCon US 2026 Videos Are Out
issues.html:
News

Python 3.15.2, 3.14.10, 3.13.18, 3.12.16, and 3.11.18 are out

A second round of expedited security releases, five days after the last: the ssl module now blocks the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA keys outright, so pip is protected even before you upgrade it. They also fix a tarfile.tar_filter bypass using links that replace the destination and reject negative-version cookies in http.cookiejar.

Announcing PSF Community Service Award Recipients!

Five new Community Service Awards go to Abhijeet Mote, Elena Williams, Hugo van Kemenade, Kevin Horn, and Sarah Abderemane. Two are familiar Django names: Elena organized the second Django Girls event ever held and now sits on Django's Code of Conduct committee, and Sarah co-founded Djangonaut Space, maintains djangoproject.com, and served as DSF Vice President in 2025.

Django Software Foundation

Natalia Bidart - Planned short-term leave

After more than three years as a Django Fellow, Natalia is taking November through January off to rest and recover, with the other Fellows and Django's teams and working groups covering in the meantime. She returns in February, ready to serve as release manager for Django 2028.

Python Software Foundation

Higher limits for organization projects

Projects owned by a PyPI organization now get 200 MB per file and 20 GB per project, double the personal limits, with nothing to turn on. Move a project out of the organization and it drops back, though any increase support already granted stays in place.

PyPI now limits versions to 128 characters

New uploads need a normalized version of 128 characters or less. Only 2 of PyPI's roughly 9.9 million releases are that long, existing releases are untouched, and pip and uv need no changes.

Wagtail CMS News

A Wagtail demo in your browser

Thibaud Colas's bakerydemo-webassembly runs Django, Wagtail, and the whole demo site in your browser with Pyodide, saving data to IndexedDB so nothing leaves your device. Log in at /admin/ with admin / changeme: it's a sandbox for learning and demos, not production.

Wagtail and the eMudhra CA key compromise

Wagtail makes outbound HTTPS calls through requests, which trusts certifi's bundled certificates rather than your operating system's, so an OS update alone won't stop it trusting eMudhra. Jake Howard covers what to upgrade, and if you deploy in containers, a rebuild picks up the patched base images.

Updates to Django

Today, "Updates to Django" is presented by Hwayoung from Djangonaut Space! 🚀

Last week we had 21 pull requests merged into Django by 13 different contributors - including 4 first-time contributors! Congratulations to gerry132, Helmi Lakhder, Aman Kumar Jain and Sanskar Kharya for having their first commits merged into Django - welcome on board!

News in Django:

  • Django 6.1 now supports Python 3.15 (#36664).
  • Fixed a bug in Django 6.2 where CSP directives containing only CSP.NONCE were omitted when the nonce was unused, potentially allowing a less restrictive fallback policy. These directives now emit 'none' instead (#37395).
  • Improved accessibility of the Unix/Windows console tabs in Django’s documentation, adding keyboard navigation and improving support for high contrast mode and right-to-left languages (#35874).

Django Fellow Reports

Django Fellow Report - Jacob

Jacob spent much of the week on security patches but still merged initial support for the HTTP QUERY method and approved Sarah's final tweaks to multiline template tags. He also marked a FETCH_PEERS bug that can overwrite deferred-field changes as a release blocker.

Django Fellow Report - Sarah

Sarah added a pull request limit for new contributors, part of her proposed Trac changes to curb irresponsible AI-led contributions, and added a "Low" severity to Trac. She also authored fixes for CSP nonces on streaming responses and overly broad permissions in file_move_safe(), and engaged in six security issues.

Django Fellow Report - Natalia

Wrapping up before her break, Natalia landed the first stage of the docs' console tab accessibility improvements and the 6.1 release note for RedirectURLMixin. She also fixed makemessages with non-ASCII filenames on Windows, escaped database errors logged by Q.check(), and patched a confirmed low-severity security issue.

Sponsored

Django for Beginners, 6th Edition

The sixth edition is out now, available in digital and paperback formats. It features two new chapters, completely updated for Django 6.1+, and more. Read the first four chapters for free to try it out.

Articles

Django as a simple static site builder

Radiac wires nanodjango, django-nanopages, and django-distill into a Django-native answer to Jekyll: app.pages("/", path="pages") maps Markdown and HTML files onto URLs with frontmatter for titles and templates, and distill renders the lot to static output. A PEP 723 block means uv run website.py needs no install first.

How I decide which Python and Django versions I want to support

Matthias Kestenholz keeps projects and dev machines on the newest Python, but supports old versions in libraries for as long as it's cheap, since people on managed hosting can't always upgrade. He drops a version only to trim CI time or to use a new feature, which currently puts most of his packages at Python 3.10+ and Django 3.2 or 4.2+.

What Our Djangonauts Shipped on Django Packages

A long-overdue tour of what three Djangonaut Space contributors, Farhan Ali Raza, Felipe de Morais, and Victoria Cruces, built in summer 2024: one-click htmx favorites you can share on your profile, a Most Liked Packages page, OpenSearch so you can search from the address bar, and documentation links pulled from PyPI. Every one of their PRs is listed at the end.

Why use open source at all with AI?

Tim Schilling had AI build a clunky but free teleprompter in six prompts, which made him ask why anyone needs open source now. His answer: quality comes from deliberating over decisions and edge cases, which AI can't do for you, and open source lets you inherit years of that deliberation for free.

Python's experimental JIT to be removed

The Steering Council gave the JIT team six months to get a standards-track PEP accepted or see the JIT removed from CPython's main branch. After the council asked for more on platform parity, user-visible behavior changes, and security, the authors withdrew PEP 836 on October 19, so the JIT is likely to come out early in the 3.16 cycle.

CSS-Tricks has a new owner!

Four years after DigitalOcean bought it from Chris Coyier, CSS-Tricks is independent again under longtime editor Geoff Graham, who is making it his full-time job. Expect one or two articles most weeks, a beginner HTML/CSS course, memberships, the return of the newsletter, and a reopened guest writing form.

Events

Django Day São Paulo 2027

São Paulo's first event dedicated entirely to Django is coming in the first half of 2027. Over the next few weeks the organizers will announce the official date and venue, open the call for speakers, and start ticket sales, so follow them on Mastodon for updates.

Podcasts

Talk Python #567: Personal AI Agents for Pythonistas

Our own Jeff Triplett joins Michael Kennedy to talk about Hermes, the self-hosted Python agent you program by talking to it, which runs 24/7 on a box at home and wakes every 15 minutes to handle chores like morning briefings. Jeff runs his on a spare Mac Mini and a few Orange Pi boards, and it now talks to Django News, DjangoTV, and the Django Job Board over MCP.

Real Python Podcast #316: The Future of Python Security

Seth Larson, the PSF's Security Developer in Residence, explains how PEP 811 formalized the Python Security Response Team's reporting and triage, and how LLMs are driving up the volume of vulnerability reports. He also covers trusted publishing on PyPI, SBOMs under PEP 770, and practical advice for locking down your CI/CD.

Videos

DjangoCon Europe 2026

The talks from Athens are now on DjangoTV, including both keynotes, auto-prefetching with Django 6.1's field fetch modes, partitioning very large tables with PostgreSQL, shipping Django as a desktop app, and a community conversation on Django and AI.

DjangoCon US 2026

The Chicago videos are out too: Karen Tracey's keynote on Django 6, Natalia Bidart on HTMX without betraying your Django views, the Django/FastAPI debate, search-as-you-type across 54 million names, and Will Vincent on modern Django deployments, plus hallway interviews with the community.

Django Job Board

Two new roles at webbyfox consultancy lead the board this week, alongside the PSF's CPython Developer in Residence opening and senior Python seats at Camden Kelly Staffing and Manychat in Barcelona.

Senior Python Engineer at webbyfox consultancy 🆕

AI Engineer at webbyfox consultancy 🆕

CPython Developer in Residence at Python Software Foundation

Senior Software Engineer (Python, React & AI) at Camden Kelly Staffing

Senior Python Engineer (Barcelona-based / Relocation support to Barcelona) at Manychat

Projects

Static Site Generators

The Django Packages grid for turning a Django site into flat HTML you can host on a CDN or GitHub Pages with no Django process running. django-distill leads on stars, django-bakery on forks, and django-freeze saw the most recent release, with django-nanopages the newest arrival at beta.
